source_text: Non coquetur fermentatum. Fermentum malitiae expurga. Azymi sinceritatis.
orientation: Origen is applying the rules for the grain offering to the moral life of the believer, moving from the broken vessel and scoured bronze to the command about leaven.
pass_a_gloss: It shall not be cooked leavened. Purge out the leaven of malice. Unleavened things of sincerity.

choices.english: It shall not be cooked leavened
choices.why: Keeps the passive future force of coquetur and the adjectival force of fermentatum, matching the legal prohibition in the source.
rejected: Do not cook it with leaven
It is not to be baked leavened

choices.english: Purge out the leaven of malice
choices.why: Expurga is a direct imperative, and the genitive malitiae is kept as 'of malice' to preserve the Pauline echo of 1 Corinthians 5:7-8.
Azymi is a genitive singular adjective used substantivally; the genitive sinceritatis is kept as 'of sincerity' to mirror the source's compressed phrase.

pass_b_english: It shall not be cooked with leaven. Purge out the leaven of malice. Be the unleavened bread of sincerity.

problems.source_quote: Non coquetur fermentatum. Fermentum malitiae expurga. Azymi sinceritatis.
problems.why: No scripture citation in source; English adds 1 Cor 5:7-8 without source warrant.
problems.ruling: Source has no citation; English adds (1 Corinthians 5:7-8) without source warrant.

edits.old: Purge out the leaven of malice (1 Corinthians 5:7-8).
edits.new: Purge out the leaven of malice.

fixed: Removed the parenthetical citation '(1 Corinthians 5:7-8)' because the source contains no scripture citation; the English added it without warrant.

last_rejected.quote: Be the unleavened bread of sincerity
last_rejected.why: Source is descriptive/adjectival ('unleavened [bread] of sincerity'), not imperative; 'Be' changes grammar to command
last_rejected.ruling: Azymi sinceritatis echoes 1 Cor 5:8 'azymis sinceritatis', understood as imperative 'be unleavened bread of sincerity' in this liturgical context.
